newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Bhutto says her party will sweep polls.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Bhutto says her party will sweep polls.

text.p: Pakistan's ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto said on Friday her party would sweep the general election set for February 3.

"February 3 will be the day of victory for the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) and the day of defeat for Leghari," she said in reference to President Farooq Leghari, who dissolved the National Assembly (lower house) and dismissed her three-year-old government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
A caretaker government has since been ruling the country.
"Rigging will not work this time," she told her party's first election rally in Karachi, referring to the 1990 elections.
Bhutto had earlier said that the results were manipulated in those elections, enabling her arch-rival Nawaz Sharif to clinch victory.
"Neither Pakistan nor the PPP is going to fall apart. It will be Leghari and the enemies of Pakistan who will be shattered on February 3," she told the rally.

The rally was organised in Karachi's western district of Baldia Town, the constituency from where Bhutto's former interior minister Naseerullah Babar is contesting against former cricket star Imran Khan.

On Thursday, Bhutto said there had been the perception that the PPP could not launch a proper election campaign because of uncertainty about the polls and also because of her petition now being heard by the Supreme Court.
Bhutto is seeking the restoration of the 217-seat National Assembly and her government.
But she said the party had now started a fully fledged campaign as the court would not reach a verdict before the poll date.
